subject: history_social
notes: The Shalimar Gardens in Lahore were built in 1641–1642 under the Mughal emperor Shah Jahan.
The gardens are laid out on three descending terraces.
In 1981 they were named a UNESCO World Heritage Site together with Lahore Fort.
stem: The student wants to emphasize the age of the gardens to an audience unfamiliar with them. Which choice most effectively uses relevant information from the notes to accomplish this goal?

choices.A: Built in 1641–1642 under the Mughal emperor Shah Jahan, the Shalimar Gardens in Lahore are nearly four centuries old.
choices.B: The Shalimar Gardens contain more than 400 fountains spread across three terraces.
choices.C: In 1981, the Shalimar Gardens and Lahore Fort were named a UNESCO World Heritage Site.
choices.D: The Shalimar Gardens in Lahore are laid out on three descending terraces.

explanation.why: The goal has two parts: stress how old the gardens are, and introduce them to readers who do not know them. Only a choice that names the gardens, says where they are, and gives the building date does both.
explanation.A: Correct. It identifies the gardens and their location for a new audience and stresses their age with the 1641–1642 date.
explanation.B: Incorrect. The fountains and terraces describe the gardens' layout, not their age.
explanation.C: Incorrect. 1981 is when the gardens were recognized, not when they were built, so it does not show their age.
explanation.D: Incorrect. This describes the layout and says nothing about age.

checks.note: Best fit on the text alone.
